requirements.statement: Each status message that presents a suggestion or warns of an error is contained in an element that takes the alert role.

citations.quote: Chaque message de statut qui présente une suggestion, ou avertit de l’existence d’une erreur utilise-t-il l’attribut WAI-ARIA `role="alert"` ?

routes.statement: The element containing the message has role="alert".
The element containing the message has aria-live="assertive" and aria-atomic="true", which may stand for the alert role when the message's nature fits it.

citations.quote: Un attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-live="assertive"` et un attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-atomic="true"` associés à un message de statut peuvent valoir pour un rôle WAI-ARIA `alert`.

rationale.text: The methodology is the one of test 7.5.1, whose fourth step covers this test. The requirement has two routes: role="alert" on the element holding the message, or aria-live="assertive" with aria-atomic="true", which the technical note accepts for a message whose nature fits. Whether content is a status message, and whether it presents a suggestion or warns of an error rather than a success or progress, is judgment that the methodology leaves to the auditor. Error messages and suggestions also appear only after the user acts, typically after a form is submitted or a field is left. So the candidate is none and no check is linked. No axe rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment: whether the page produces such messages is not known from the page as loaded. Needs is state, since these messages follow an action.
